## Add persistent storage to a Cluster

You can add persistent storage to an `ACTIVE` cluster with:

```
clever k8s add-persistent-storage myKubeCluster
```

Once added you can't remove it, but you can start a fresh cluster without persistent storage.

## Get kubeconfig file of a Cluster

To get the `kubeconfig` file of an `ACTIVE` cluster, and set it as the current context, use:

```
clever k8s get-kubeconfig myKubeCluster
clever k8s get-kubeconfig myKubeCluster > ~/.kube/config
```

I haven't added `clever k8s update` yet. Creating `src/commands/k8s/k8s.update.command.js` needs write permission, which wasn't granted. I didn't try to get around that through the shell. I also reverted the one edit that did go through (registering the command in `global.commands.js`), so the working tree is clean again.

**What I found:** the API call already exists. `k8sUpdate()` in `src/lib/k8s.js` sends a PATCH request that can change the cluster's name, description, tags and features, but no command uses it yet.

**What the command will do** (modeled on `oauth-consumers update`):

```bash
clever k8s update <cluster-id|cluster-name> [--name <name>] [--description <description>] \
  [--tag <tag[,tag...]>] [--autoscaling enabled|disabled] [--org <org>] [--format json]
```

- It only sends the fields you pass. With no options, it fails with "Nothing to update, use at least one of --name, --description, --tag or --autoscaling".
- `--tag` replaces the current tags and uses the same parser as `k8s create`.
- `--autoscaling` takes `enabled` or `disabled` rather than an on/off switch, so it can turn the autoscaler off as well as on.
- Persistent storage is left out because it already has its own command and can't be turned off.
- `since: null`, and it inherits the `k8s` feature flag from the parent command.

**Two things to check:**
- Whether the API accepts `features.autoscalingEnabled` in an update is taken from a code comment on `k8sUpdate()`, not checked against the API docs. Tell me if you'd rather drop `--autoscaling` for now.
- The project requires an existing issue for every PR. I haven't opened one or looked for one.

If you grant write access (or ask me to retry), I'll create the file, register it, and add examples to `docs/kubernetes.md` and the `k8s` feature-flag instructions in `src/config/features.js`. Then I'll run `npm run docs` and `npm run validate`, and check `--help` with `node bin/clever.js`. I won't run a real update without your go-ahead, since it would change a production cluster.
